meta.scene_summary: We are burning down the forest to power the memes, only to find the fire alarm is also broken.

cooking.headline: We're burning the entire state of Michigan just to generate cat memes.
cooking.summary: Four hundred data centers are now consuming more electricity than an entire U.S. state, which is a bold strategy for the planet.
cooking.plain_english: A small group of 400 large data centers now uses more total electricity than the entire state of Michigan.

cooking.headline: The Tor Project is playing Whac-A-Mole with a DDoS attack
cooking.summary: Tor is fighting off a massive, sustained traffic spike by pushing out a rapid-response security patch. It is basically the digital equivalent of trying to fix a leaky faucet while the entire neighborhood is trying to use your bathroom at once.
cooking.plain_english: The Tor Project has released a software update to protect its network from a large-scale attempt to overwhelm it with fake traffic.

cooking.headline: Qwen4-Max dropped, making your current LLM feel like a calculator from 2005
cooking.summary: Every few weeks a new model claims to be the smartest thing in the room, which is great until you realize your GPU budget is crying for help. It's the tech equivalent of a high school student winning a Nobel Prize every Tuesday.
cooking.plain_english: Alibaba has released a new, highly advanced artificial intelligence model called Qwen4-Max.

cooking.headline: Active Directory is finally being retired, or at least that's what we keep telling ourselves
cooking.summary: We've been trying to break up with Active Directory for decades, but it's the toxic ex that just refuses to move out of the infrastructure. Maybe this time we'll actually make the switch, provided we don't accidentally delete the entire company's access permissions first.
cooking.plain_english: New identity management systems are replacing the traditional Active Directory framework for authenticating machines and users.

cooked.headline: United Airlines discovers that 'high availability' is just a suggestion
cooked.summary: United Airlines suffered a massive system outage, proving that even global aviation still runs on hope and legacy middleware. It turns out that when your scheduling software decides to take an unscheduled vacation, thousands of passengers get to join it.
cooked.plain_english: United Airlines experienced a major technical failure that disrupted their flight operations and caused widespread delays.

cooked.headline: Optimizely got 'optimized' by hackers injecting a skimmer
cooked.summary: Optimizely was compromised, allowing attackers to inject malicious code directly into their platform's delivery chain. It is the ultimate irony when the tool meant for A/B testing your site ends up running a live experiment on your users' payment data.
cooked.plain_english: Hackers gained access to Optimizely's systems to insert malicious software that steals information from websites using their services.

cooked.headline: Microsoft's fix for a bug just became the bug
cooked.summary: Microsoft confirmed that a massive email outage was caused by a software defect they accidentally introduced while trying to fix a previous issue in July. It's the digital equivalent of trying to fix a leaky faucet and accidentally flooding the entire neighborhood instead.
cooked.plain_english: Microsoft experienced a significant email service disruption because of an error in a software update designed to resolve a prior problem.

cooked.headline: JPMorgan Chase just reminded us that money is basically just a database row
cooked.summary: A technical glitch at JPMorgan Chase caused widespread banking delays across multiple US institutions, proving once again that our entire financial system is held together by hope and legacy code. It turns out that when the database goes down, your net worth becomes purely theoretical.
cooked.plain_english: A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase resulted in transaction processing delays that affected multiple American banks.

cooked.headline: The job market is currently doing a very convincing impression of a desert.
cooked.summary: Hiring posts are at a 12-year low while AI handles half the workload, proving we've successfully automated ourselves out of a paycheck. It's a great time to be a GPU, but a terrible time to be a junior dev looking for their first commit.
cooked.plain_english: Job openings are at a twelve-year low as artificial intelligence tools are now being used to perform half of all job tasks.

cooked.headline: uBlock Origin's element picker just became a security hole
cooked.summary: The tool designed to help you nuke annoying website ads accidentally created a path for malicious scripts to run in your browser. It turns out that giving a browser extension the power to pick and choose elements is a great way to let attackers pick your pockets instead.
cooked.plain_english: A security vulnerability was discovered in the uBlock Origin browser extension that could allow malicious websites to execute unauthorized code.
